record.title: The denominator conjecture for corolla coefficients
record.statement:
Let $\mathtt{Crl}_n$ denote the corolla with $n$ leaves, let $\sympawn_{\mathtt{Crl}_n}$ be its coefficient, and let $\Phi_d$ denote the $d$th cyclotomic polynomial. **The denominator conjecture.** The denominator of $\sympawn_{\mathtt{Crl}_n}$ is

$$
\prod_{d=2}^{n+1}\Phi_d.
$$

This conjecture concerns the regularity of the denominators of coefficients associated with corollas; the surrounding discussion gives examples and notes that the observed denominators appear simple and regular. No resolution is given in the source.
record.source_name: Frédéric Chapoton, “Sur une série en arbres à deux paramètres”, arXiv:1301.1843 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1301.1843

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2013).

record.title: The cyclotomic divisibility conjecture for odd tree powers
record.statement:
Let $\lambda=(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_m)$ be a partition, let $T_\lambda$ be the rooted tree with $n+1$ vertices defined by

$$
T_\lambda=\textsc{B}_{+}(\mathtt{Lnr}_{\lambda_1},\ldots,\mathtt{Lnr}_{\lambda_m}),
$$

let $k\geq 3$ be an odd integer, and let $\Phi_d$ denote the $d$th cyclotomic polynomial. **The cyclotomic divisibility conjecture.** The coefficient $\Omega_{q,\textsc{B}_{+}(T_\lambda^k)}$ is divisible by $\Phi_{1+\max\lambda}$.

This conjecture concerns cyclotomic factors in coefficients of the series $\Omega_q$ associated with trees constructed from partitions. The source gives no evidence of a resolution.
record.source_name: Frédéric Chapoton, “Sur une série en arbres à deux paramètres”, arXiv:1301.1843 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1301.1843

record.title: Geodesic strengthenings of the Norine and Feder–Subi conjectures
record.statement: Let $Q_n$ be the $n$-dimensional hypercube, with edge set $E(Q_n)$, and let a **geodesic** be a shortest path in $Q_n$. For a $2$-colouring of $E(Q_n)$, call it **antipodal** if no two antipodal edges receive the same colour. **Geodesic strengthening conjectures.** The following statements hold: (A) Every antipodal colouring $c$ of $E(Q_n)$ contains a monochromatic geodesic between some pair of antipodal vertices. (B) In every $2$-colouring $c$ of $E(Q_n)$, there is a geodesic between antipodal points which changes colour at most once. These are proposed as geodesic strengthenings of the two preceding conjectures. The source gives no resolution and only notes that the preceding theorem establishes a weaker monochromatic-geodesic result at length $\lceil n/2\rceil$.
record.source_name: Imre Leader and Eoin Long, “Long geodesics in subgraphs of the cube”, arXiv:1301.2195 (2013).

record.title: The single-valuedness conjecture for two-dimensional graphical functions
record.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a graph, and let $f^{(0)}_\Gamma$ denote its two-dimensional graphical function. Let ${\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{sv}}$ be the algebra of single-valued functions defined in the source.

**Single-valued graphical-function conjecture.** For any graph $\Gamma$,

$$
f^{(0)}_\Gamma\in {\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{sv}}.
$$

This predicts that two-dimensional graphical functions belong to the single-valued function algebra. The claim is used later to conjecture single-valuedness of periods of completed primitive graphs.
record.source_name: Oliver Schnetz, “Graphical functions and single-valued multiple polylogarithms”, arXiv:1302.6445 (2014).

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of February 2013). “Finally, the zig-zag conjecture is proved in using corollary .”

record.title: Triangular interval conjecture for exactly-coloured infinite subgraphs
record.statement:
Let $\Delta:\mathbb{N}^{(2)}\twoheadrightarrow[k]$ be a surjective $k$-colouring, and let $\mathcal{F}_{\Delta}$ denote the set of numbers of colours appearing on infinite induced complete subgraphs. Suppose that $n\geq2$ is a natural number and $k\geq\binom{n}{2}+2$. **Triangular interval conjecture.** Then

$$
\mathcal{F}_{\Delta}\cap\left(\left[\binom{n+1}{2}+1\right]\backslash\left[\binom{n}{2}+1\right]\right)\neq\emptyset.
$$

If true, this would imply the paper's main theorem. The case $n=2$ follows from a stated corollary, and the first non-trivial instance is proved when $k\geq5$, with $\mathcal{F}_{\Delta}\cap\{5,6,7\}\neq\emptyset$; the general case remains open.
record.source_name: Bhargav Narayanan, “Exactly m-coloured complete infinite subgraphs”, arXiv:1303.2103 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1303.2103

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2013). “The problem of determining $\psi$ completely is of course still open.”

record.title: The extremal conjecture for separated list chromatic number
record.statement:
For integers $c,n\ge 1$, let $G$ be a graph with $n$ vertices, and let $\chi_l(G,c)$ denote its list chromatic number with separation $c$. **Extremal conjecture.**

$$
\chi_l(G,c)\le \chi_l(K_n,c).
$$

This conjecture asserts that among all $n$-vertex graphs, the complete graph maximizes the list chromatic number with separation $c$. The source provides no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Zoltan Furedi, Alexandr Kostochka and Mohit Kumbhat, “Minimal abundant packings and choosability with separation”, arXiv:1303.4030 (2024).

record.title: Francisco–Hà–Van Tuyl's expansion conjecture for critically chromatic graphs
record.statement: Let $G$ be a graph that is **critically $s$-chromatic**, meaning that its chromatic number is $s$ and deleting any vertex lowers the chromatic number. For a subset $W$ of the vertices of $G$, let $G[W]$ denote the graph obtained by expanding every vertex of $W$ into two adjacent vertices, each inheriting all the original neighbors. **Francisco–Hà–Van Tuyl's expansion conjecture.** There exists a subset $W$ of the vertices of $G$ such that $G[W]$ is critically $(s+1)$-chromatic. This conjecture is proposed as a possible approach to proving persistence for cover ideals of imperfect graphs; the source gives affirmative persistence results for odd holes and odd antiholes but does not state a resolution of the expansion conjecture.
record.source_name: Christopher A. Francisco, Huy Tai Ha and Jeffrey Mermin, “Powers of squarefree monomial ideals and combinatorics”, arXiv:1303.6642 (2013).

record.title: The two-piece monochromatic path and cycle covering conjecture for 3-colored complete graphs
record.statement:
Let $K_n$ be a complete graph whose edges are colored with three colors. A **monochromatic path or cycle** is a path or cycle all of whose edges have one color, and the two pieces are required to be vertex disjoint. **The two-piece covering conjecture.** There are two vertex-disjoint monochromatic paths, or two vertex-disjoint monochromatic cycles, covering at least

$$
\frac{6n}{7}
$$

of the vertices. The paper proves only a weaker matching statement, so this remains open there.
record.source_name: András Gyárfás, Gábor N. Sárközy and Stanley Selkow, “Coverings by few monochromatic pieces - a transition between two Ramsey problems”, arXiv:1304.0871 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1304.0871

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2013).

record.title: The monochromatic tree-cover averaging conjecture
record.statement:
Let $t$ be a positive integer, let $s$ satisfy $1\le s\le t-1$, and let $K_n$ be a complete graph with its edges colored using $t$ colors. A **monochromatic tree** is a tree all of whose edges have one color. **The averaging conjecture.** At least

$$
\frac{ns}{t-1}
$$

vertices can be covered by the vertices of at most $s$ monochromatic trees. This follows from the preceding Ryser-type conjecture by an averaging argument, and is therefore open in the same generality.
record.source_name: András Gyárfás, Gábor N. Sárközy and Stanley Selkow, “Coverings by few monochromatic pieces - a transition between two Ramsey problems”, arXiv:1304.0871 (2013).

record.title: Generic mechanical non-domination conjecture for chain-recurrence classes
record.statement:
Let $f$ be a $C^r$ diffeomorphism, let $P$ be a saddle, and let $\mathcal C(P,f)$ be its chain-recurrent class. The class is **mechanically without domination of index $i$** when a cycle of basic sets containing $P$ contains a mechanical obstruction to domination of index $i$.

**Generic mechanical non-domination conjecture.** There is a residual subset $\mathcal R$ of $C^r$-diffeomorphisms $f$ such that if $\mathcal C(P,f)$ is not dominated of index $i$, then it has $C^r$-robustly mechanically no domination of index $i$.

This conjecture proposes that generic failures of dominated splittings arise from identifiable mechanisms such as non-simple Lyapunov spectra, tangencies, or bundle tangencies. The source gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Nicolas Gourmelon, “Steps towards a classification of C^r-generic dynamics close to homoclinic points”, arXiv:1410.1758 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1410.1758

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2014).

record.title: Finiteness conjecture for game distinguishing numbers
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, and let $D_\mathcal{G}(G)$ and $D_\mathcal{R}(G)$ denote its Gentle-game and Rascal-game distinguishing numbers. An **automorphism of order $2$** is an automorphism whose order is exactly $2$. **Finiteness conjecture.** If $G$ has no automorphism of order $2$, then

$$
D_\mathcal{G}(G)\text{ and }D_\mathcal{R}(G)\text{ are both finite}.
$$

The conjecture proposes a characterization-related sufficient condition for the two game distinguishing numbers to be finite; the paper describes the broader characterization as a challenging open problem.
record.source_name: Sylvain Gravier, Kahina Meslem, Simon Schmidt and Souad Slimani, “A New Game Invariant of Graphs: the Game Distinguishing Number”, arXiv:1410.3359 (2017).

record.title: Richness of binary projections of episturmian words
record.statement:
Let $\mathbf u$ be an episturmian word over an alphabet $\mathcal A$, and let $\zeta$ be a binary projection from $\mathcal A$.

**Projection richness conjecture.** The word $\zeta(\mathbf u)$ is rich.

This generalizes the preceding result for ternary Arnoux--Rauzy words, whose binary projections are shown to be rich. The statement is suggested by computer experiments, but no proof or disproof is given here.

record.title: Extra-special orbit and Lagrangian-ideal conjecture
record.statement:
In the extra-special case, let $\mathfrak X_{\Delta(1)}$ be the reverse operator on the associated weight poset, let $\Pi_l$ be the set of long simple roots, and let $h$ be the Coxeter number.

**Extra-special orbit conjecture.** The number of $\mathfrak X_{\Delta(1)}$-orbits is $\#\Pi_l$, every orbit has size $h-1$, and, if $h$ is even, every orbit contains a unique Lagrangian upper ideal.

The orbit count and orbit size are suggested by the proved enumeration in the extra-special case and explicit calculations; the statement is verified in several types but remains open in general.

record.title: The improved diameter and order bounds for cubic graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a cubic graph, and let $D$ be its diameter. The **cubic-graph algebraic-connectivity bound conjecture.** Its algebraic connectivity satisfies

$$
\lambda_{2}(G)\leq 3-2^{3/2}\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{D}\right).
$$

Moreover, if $G$ has order $n=2^{K+1}-2$, then

$$
\lambda_{2}(G)\leq 3-2^{3/2}\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{K}\right).
$$

These conjectured bounds are numerical improvements over the cited Nilli bound and are posed as open conjectures in the source.

record.title: The coefficient-polynomial conjecture for Type A and Type BIII sums
record.statement:
At $q=1$, write the Type A and Type BIII sums as 
$$
S^{\mathrm{A}}_{N}=\sum_{i=0}^{N}S_{N,i}Q^{i},\qquad S^{\mathrm{BIII}}_{N}=\sum_{i=0}^{N}S'_{N,i}(Q+Q^{-1})^{i},
$$
 with nonnegative integer coefficients $S_{N,i}$ and $S'_{N,i}$. **Coefficient-polynomial conjecture.** The coefficients satisfy 
$$
S_{N,i}=S_{N,N-i}=S'_{N,i}=S'_{N,N-i},
$$
 and 
$$
S_{N,i}=\left(\prod_{k=0}^{i-1}\frac{N-k}{2k+2}\right)P_i(N),\qquad P_i(N)=N^i+\sum_{j=0}^{i-1}p_{i,j}N^j,
$$
 where $p_{i,j}\in\mathbb{Z}$. The source presents this as an empirical conjecture and lists the first few polynomials; no proof or resolution is given.

record.title: The Type A symmetric-binary-matrix coefficient conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}_N$ be the set of symmetric binary $N\times N$ matrices with no row sum greater than one. For $a=(a_{i,j})$, define 
$$
\operatorname{wt}(a)=\#\{a_{i,j}=1\mid i\leq j\}.
$$
 Let $S_{N,i}$ be the coefficient of $Q^i$ in the Type A sum at $q=1$. **Type A matrix conjecture.** 
$$
S_{N,i}=\#\{a\in\mathcal{A}_N\mid \operatorname{wt}(a)=i\}.
$$
 This refines the total-sum enumeration by predicting a weight-preserving interpretation of every coefficient; the source does not provide a proof or resolution.

record.title: The odd-order near-factor characterization conjecture
record.statement: Let $v=2n+1$ be an odd integer, let $K_v$ be the complete graph on $\{0,1,\ldots,v-1\}$, and let $L$ be a list of $n$ positive integers not exceeding $n$. A near $1$-factor $F$ is a set of $n$ pairwise disjoint edges, and $\ell(F)$ is its list of edge-lengths. **The near-factor characterization conjecture.** There exists a near $1$-factor $F$ of $K_v$ such that $\ell(F)=L$ if and only if, for any divisor $d$ of $v$, the number of multiples of $d$ appearing in $L$ does not exceed $\frac{v-d}{2}$. This is presented as a generalization of Bacher's problem for odd order. The supplied text gives no resolution.
record.source_name: M. Meszka, A. Pasotti and M. A. Pellegrini, “The seating couple problem in even case”, arXiv:2308.16553 (2023).
record.references:

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.16553

record.title: Babai spectrum conjecture for paths
record.statement:
Let $n$ and $k$ be fixed positive integers with

$$
\left\lfloor \frac{n}{2} \right\rfloor < k \leq n-1,
$$

and let $m\in\{2,3,\ldots,n-1\}$ be the unique integer satisfying

$$
n-\left\lceil \frac{n}{m} \right\rceil < k \leq n-\left\lceil \frac{n}{m+1} \right\rceil.
$$

For the path $P_n$ and its $k$-Babai spectrum $\operatorname{Spec}(P_n,k)$, the preceding theorem gives

$$
\{m+1,m+2,\ldots,k+1\}\subseteq \operatorname{Spec}(P_n,k).
$$

**Babai spectrum conjecture for paths.** Under these hypotheses,

$$
\operatorname{Spec}(P_n,k)=\{m+1,m+2,\ldots,k+1\}.
$$

The conjecture strengthens the preceding theorem's inclusion to an exact description of the Babai spectrum. The authors say that numerical examples motivate it, but no resolution is supplied in the source.
record.source_name: Peter Johnson, Celalettin Kaya and Ryan W. Matzke, “Babai Numbers and Babai Spectra of Paths and Cycles”, arXiv:2409.04869 (2024).
record.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2014–2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2005.02797](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.02797), [arXiv:1412.1438](https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.1438).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.04869

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2024).

record.title: Bondy's small cycle double cover conjecture
record.statement:
A **cycle double cover** of a graph is a list of cycles such that every edge belongs to exactly two of them. A graph is **simple** if it has no loops or parallel edges, and **$2$-edge-connected** if deleting any one edge leaves it connected.

**Bondy's small cycle double cover conjecture.** Every simple $2$-edge-connected graph on $n$ vertices has a cycle double cover consisting of at most $n-1$ cycles.

The bound is best possible for complete graphs. The source notes that this conjecture does not follow immediately from its proof of the cycle double cover theorem.
record.source_name: Sang-il Oum, “A proof of the cycle double cover conjecture by OpenAI: An exposition”, arXiv:2607.16356 (2026).
record.references:

The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2606.03696](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.03696), [arXiv:2503.15950](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.15950), [arXiv:1705.07066](https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.07066), [arXiv:1402.4268](https://arxiv.org/abs/1402.4268).

record.title: Symmetric basis conjecture for eigenvectors of generators on \(\ell_p\)
record.statement:
Let $A$ be the generator of a $C_0$-group on $\ell_p$, with $p>1$, whose eigenvalues, counted with multiplicity, are $\{\lambda_n\}_{n=1}^{\infty}$ and whose corresponding normalized eigenvectors are $\{e_n\}_{n=1}^{\infty}$. Assume that

$$
\overline{\operatorname{Lin}}\{e_n\}_{n=1}^{\infty}=\ell_p.
$$

Also assume that the point spectrum $\{\lambda_n\}_{n=1}^{\infty}$ satisfies condition (2). **Symmetric basis conjecture.** Then $\{e_n\}_{n=1}^{\infty}$ forms a symmetric basis of $\ell_p$. This proposes an extension of the preceding result for operators with symmetric basis families of eigenvectors and would characterize the eigenvectors under the stated spectral and completeness hypotheses; no resolution is given in the source.
record.source_name: Grigory M. Sklyar and Vitalii Marchenko, “Hardy inequality and the construction of infinitesimal operators with non-basis family of eigenvectors”, arXiv:1405.2731 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1405.2731

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2014).
